instruction: Configure the power button in power settings so that it does nothing when pressed.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing the power button action to 'Nothing' in GNOME power settings. The evaluator checks if 'gsettings get org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.power power-button-action' returns "'nothing'" (note the single quotes in the string value). This uses existing evaluator functions (exact_match metric and vm_command_line getter) - no custom functions needed.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Binary scoring: 1.0 if power-button-action is set to 'nothing', 0.0 otherwise

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator uses the correct gsettings command to retrieve the power button action setting (org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.power power-button-action)
Expected value correctly matches gsettings output format: "'nothing'\n" includes both the single quotes that gsettings uses for string values and the trailing newline from command output
Exact match comparison is semantically appropriate for this binary setting verification
Complete coverage: instruction requires setting power button to 'Nothing', evaluator checks exactly this requirement
No state accessibility issues: gsettings values are persistent system settings that don't require UI to be open, no postconfig needed
Proper error handling: if command fails or returns different value, exact_match returns 0.0
